result.summary:
Independently re-derived from docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md itself (not CODE-DESIGNER's step-01-code-designer.json result.summary), against the live requirement text (docs/agents/requirements.yaml lines 1184-1227), the live schema (apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts), and the live implementation of withdrawRegistration/registerForEvent/decideWithdrawOutcome (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts) and isFinished/computeSeatsLeft/buildSeatsLine/getFlowUserByTgId (domain/event.ts, domain/user.ts).

1. ZERO IMPLEMENTATION CODE (exhaustive). `grep -n '```'` finds 7 fenced pairs: lines 54-64 (prose pseudocode listing withdrawRegistration's extended step sequence -- 'step 6 (NEW) -- only when... call promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible(tx, row.eventId, at)' -- narrated in English, no if/return/comparison statement, same style REQ-022's own passed Sec2.2 narration used), 107-109 (bare `isAutoPromotionHalted(...): boolean;` signature, no body), 133-151 (PromotionEligibilityInput interface + PromotionEligibility union + decidePromotionEligibility bare signature -- the eligibility TABLE itself is stated only in Sec2.2's markdown table, never as executable branching), 170-185 (WithdrawOutcome type only), 264-271 (duplicate open/close, same WithdrawOutcome block), 332-343 (PromotionOutcome union + promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible bare signature), 404-411 (Catalog.promotion interface, three `string;` fields with trailing comments, no bodies). None contains an if/return/arithmetic/comparison statement. Sec2.1's T-24h rule and Sec2.2's eligibility table are both stated in prose/table form only ('24 hours or less remain -> halted', first-match-wins table) -- exactly the discipline .claude/agents/code-designer.md requires after the REQ-016/REQ-017 traps. No SQL as a runnable query string anywhere -- every DB operation (Sec3 steps 1-6) is one-line English description of a SELECT/UPDATE/INSERT shape.

2. TOKEN REFERENCES. `grep -n 'var(--\|--color\|--space\|--font' docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md` returns zero matches -- bot/backend design, no rendered UI, consistent with REQ-018/020/021/022 precedent; nothing to check against tokens.css.

3. AT-MOST-ONCE DOUBLE-PROCESSING -- TRACED PRECISELY, going beyond the design's own Sec5 walkthrough per this gate's instruction. Two distinct ways 'the promotion path runs twice for the same freed seat' could occur:
   (a) Direct re-invocation of promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible for the same event with no intervening withdrawal (the literal shape of AC7's stated test, and the natural unit-test surface per the REQ-009 automated-test-runner precedent AC4 already establishes for this same file). Sec5 correctly shows the second call's step 2 recomputes admittedCount fresh (already raised to capacity by the first call's committed UPDATE), so decidePromotionEligibility row 3 refuses at seatsLeft<=0 before step 4 (candidate selection) is ever reached -- no second SELECT...FOR UPDATE against registrations, no write, no send attempted. Verified computeSeatsLeft is exactly `capacity - admittedCount` (domain/event.ts line 710) confirming this recompute is live, not cached.
   (b) A duplicated/retried Telegram update causing the SAME withdraw confirm callback to be processed twice concurrently, both reaching withdrawRegistration for the SAME registrationId before the first call's transaction commits. Read the live withdrawRegistration code directly (registration.ts lines 348-401): step 1 is `SELECT ... FROM registrations WHERE id = registrationId FOR UPDATE`, inside `db.transaction`. This row lock serializes two concurrent calls on the same registrationId: the second call's own FOR UPDATE blocks until the first transaction commits (or rolls back). Once the first commits (admission now 'withdrawn'), the second call's FOR UPDATE unblocks and re-reads the row fresh -- decideWithdrawOutcome (lines 330-345) sees admission='withdrawn', which falls into the `admission !== 'requested' && !== 'waitlisted' && !== 'admitted'` branch (line 341), returning `{kind:'not-eligible', admission:'withdrawn'}` -- NOT 'withdrawn'. REQ-023's own Sec0 gate ('promotion is only attempted when the row's admission read in step 1 was admitted') is therefore never reached on the second call: it fails one level earlier, inside decideWithdrawOutcome itself, before Sec0's new step 6 branch is even evaluated. So case (b) reduces to case (a)'s already-covered no-op, not a separate gap -- confirmed by reading the actual lock discipline REQ-022 shipped, not merely trusting Sec1's 'reused unchanged' claim.
   CONCLUSION: the design's Sec5 reasoning is sound and its scope boundary (does not cover a crash between commit and the Telegram send itself, explicitly named and forwarded to REQ-025) is honestly stated, not silently assumed solved. No unaddressed gap found for AC7's stated test shape.

4. FOR UPDATE ATOMIC CAPACITY RE-CHECK FOR PROMOTION -- VERIFIED EXPLICIT. Sec3 step 1 states promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible issues its OWN `SELECT ... FROM events WHERE id = eventId FOR UPDATE` as its first operation, inside the same `tx` handle withdrawRegistration passes in (withdrawRegistration itself never locks events -- confirmed by reading registration.ts lines 348-401 in full: no `events` table reference anywhere in that function). This answers the gate's question directly: promotion acquires its own events-row lock; it does not rely on any lock withdrawRegistration might have taken (there is none). Cross-checked against the live registerForEvent (lines 109-134): its step 2 is also `SELECT events ... FOR UPDATE` as the first DB op in its own transaction, before existingRows/admittedCount are read. Both functions therefore serialize on the same shared `events` row before either computes seatsLeft -- Postgres row-lock semantics make whichever transaction commits first release the lock, and the second transaction's subsequent admittedCount COUNT is guaranteed fresh relative to the first's completed write. This is the exact mechanism AC4's concurrency test exercises; Sec3.1's deadlock argument (events is the only row both transactions ever contend for; each additionally touches only a disjoint registrations row) is correct and matches the live code's actual lock-acquisition order in both functions.

5. T-24h COMPARISON -- VERIFIED EXACT. isAutoPromotionHalted(startsAt, evaluationTime) is stated to compare (startsAt - evaluationTime) against exactly 24h, with the boundary instant itself (24h remaining exactly) landing in the HALTED bucket -- 'strictly more than 24 hours remain' is required for eligible. evaluationTime is an explicit parameter per decisions/0006, matching the live isFinished/isRegistrationOpen convention verified directly (domain/event.ts lines 717-731: both take evaluationTime as a parameter, neither calls Date.now()/new Date() internally). No SQL now()/current_timestamp appears anywhere in the design. AC1 (48h out) and AC2 (12h out) both sit clear of the boundary as the design itself notes, and the design still states the exact boundary convention precisely rather than leaving it to be guessed.

6. CANCELLED/FINISHED-EVENT REFUSAL (AC5) -- VERIFIED. decidePromotionEligibility row 1 refuses when `eventStatus !== 'published'` (covers cancelled, and defensively draft) OR `isFinished(endsAt, evaluationTime)`. Verified the live isFinished (domain/event.ts line 729): `evaluationTime.getTime() > endsAt.getTime()` -- matches AC5's exact wording ('an event whose ends_at has passed'). This check is ordered first in the table, before the T-24h/capacity checks, so a cancelled event with a non-empty waitlist and no capacity issue is still correctly refused with no registrations row ever read.

7. NOTIFICATION IGNORES broadcast_opt_in (S10) -- VERIFIED. `grep -rn 'broadcast_opt_in|broadcastOptIn' apps/bot/src` returns only schema.ts (the column definition itself) -- no handler or domain function anywhere in the current codebase reads it at all, so there is structurally nothing for Sec6.2's new send path to gate on even by omission-of-a-guard-that-already-exists-elsewhere. Sec6.2 step 2 explicitly states 'no broadcast_opt_in check anywhere in this step, by omission' and step 1's composition reads only tgId/lang (getUserForNotificationById's own return shape, Sec6.1, deliberately excludes broadcast_opt_in from what it even selects) -- confirmed the interface UserForNotification (tgId, lang, chapterDefaultLang) has no such field, so it is architecturally impossible for the send path built from this read to branch on it.

8. REUSED-FUNCTION CLAIMS SPOT-CHECKED AGAINST LIVE CODE (not trusted from the design's own assertions): computeSeatsLeft (event.ts:709-711), isFinished (event.ts:729-731), isRegistrationOpen (event.ts:717-725, confirms the 'evaluationTime as parameter' convention isAutoPromotionHalted claims to mirror), buildSeatsLine (event.ts:739-741), getFlowUserByTgId's users-left-join-chapters shape (user.ts:88-106, confirms getUserForNotificationById's claimed join shape is a real, existing pattern, just re-keyed on users.id), getEventByIdWithChapterTimezone (event.ts:752) and resolveLang (i18n/resolveLang.ts:43) both exist as named. Cross-user send claim verified: `grep -rn 'ctx.api.sendMessage|ctx.reply' apps/bot/src/handlers/*.ts` finds only ctx.reply calls everywhere today -- confirms Sec6.2's flagged claim that this is the first ctx.api.sendMessage-to-a-different-chat call site in this codebase, not an unverified assertion.

9. THE TWO MINOR ISSUES CARRIED FROM CODE-DESIGNER -- JUDGED ACCEPTABLE, NOT BLOCKING. (a) No QR delivery mechanism (Sec6.4): correctly scoped -- checked directly that composeRegistrationReply's 'admitted' case (handlers/registration.ts) already ships today with no qr_token rendering at all, so REQ-023 sending the raw token string as plain text is not a regression relative to the direct-admission path's existing fidelity; genuinely a pre-existing, cross-cutting gap, correctly deferred to a future shared-mechanism requirement rather than invented ad hoc here (which would itself be scope creep beyond this requirement's ACs). (b) /events seats-left not distinguishing halted-vs-open (Sec7): AC/requirement text only demands the freed seat be 'visible to the organizer somewhere' -- literally satisfied by the live, uncached computeSeatsLeft/buildSeatsLine recompute on every /events call (verified this call path is unconditional, no organizer gate, per event.ts). The richer 'N seats left, M waiting' view is correctly named as a Release-3 manual-promotion UI concern, out of scope for this requirement's stated ACs. Neither issue leaves an AC unaddressed.

10. AC-TO-DESIGN-ELEMENT MAP -- re-derived against the live requirement text (requirements.yaml lines 1219-1226), not trusted from Sec9's own table. AC1 (earliest-waitlisted promoted, others untouched) -> Sec3 step 4's ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE, verified this matches getWaitlistPosition's live tie-break convention. AC2 (T-24h halt) -> item 5 above. AC3 (empty waitlist, no error) -> Sec3 step 4's no-row-found branch returning a normal value, not a throw. AC4 (concurrency, no over-admit) -> item 4 above. AC5 (cancelled/finished refused) -> item 6 above. AC6 (notification ignores broadcast_opt_in) -> item 7 above. AC7 (exactly one audit row; exactly one notification on a doubled run) -> Sec3 step 6 (single writeAuditLog call, reached only on the one write-worthy branch) + item 3 above. All 7 map to concrete, non-deferred design elements; Sec8's four open questions are each named with their resolution or explicit deferral to a stated future owner, never a silent gap in an AC-relevant area.

Verdict: PASS. No check failed.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md Sec6.4: no QR *delivery* mechanism (rendered image or scannable deep link) exists anywhere in this codebase today -- confirmed the direct-registration 'admitted' reply (handlers/registration.ts composeRegistrationReply) never renders qr_token either. This design satisfies 'notified with their QR' at the same fidelity the direct path already has (raw token string as plain text). Recommend ORCH file a new issue for a future requirement to give both the direct-admission and promotion paths a single shared ticket/QR-rendering mechanism. Not blocking: pre-existing, cross-cutting gap, not introduced or worsened by this design.

docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md Sec7: /events' live seats-left count satisfies 'visible to the organizer somewhere' as literally required, but does not distinguish a T-24h-halted freed seat (with a non-empty waitlist behind it) from an ordinary never-filled seat. Left as a recommendation for a future (Release 3 manual-promotion) requirement. Not blocking: no acceptance criterion in scope asks for new UI, and the literal AC text is satisfied today.

The requirement's own description text (requirements.yaml line 1215-1216) frames the at-most-once mechanism as 'making the promotion write and the send-marker part of the same transaction', which reads as though a persisted marker gates the send. The design's actual mechanism (Sec5) has no such marker at all -- the notification is composed and sent post-commit, outside any transaction, and at-most-once instead falls out of the promotion WRITE being naturally unrepeatable (a second run finds seatsLeft<=0 and takes no write, so nothing downstream ever attempts a second send). This is functionally correct and traced sound (item 3 above), and the design explicitly names the real gap this does NOT close (a crash between commit and the Telegram send itself) rather than papering over it with the requirement's more literal 'send-marker' framing -- so this is a documentation/wording mismatch between the requirement and the design, not a functional gap. Filed for the record so REQ-ANALYST/REVIEWER are aware the requirement's descriptive language is looser than the design's precise mechanism, not because the design is wrong.
